turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I do not refer to them as misfortunes which have befallen a person who has always conducted himself with honourable intentions and met with fair dealing from the world.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I cannot speak of Mr. Wickham's misfortunes in the light of your misunderstanding. Yet, I confess, my own actions have contributed to your prejudice against me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your actions have indeed done much to foster my prejudice, Mr. Darcy. Your interference in Jane and Bingley's relationship, and your treatment of Mr. Wickham, have not been honourable.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am well aware of the faults that I have exhibited, Elizabeth. My pride and my actions have been my downfall, yet I cannot help but feel that my intentions have been misunderstood.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I understand your feelings, Mr. Darcy, but your actions speak louder than your words today. Your interference and your pride have been the cause of much unhappiness.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I acknowledge the pain my actions have caused, Elizabeth. Yet, I must express my feelings for you, though I fear they will not be met with the same sentiment.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am sorry to say, Mr. Darcy, that my feelings towards you are far from what you might hope for. Your actions have caused me great distress.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: My pride, my prejudices, have indeed been the cause of my undoing, Elizabeth. Yet, I cannot conceal my feelings any longer.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your words do not change the fact that your actions have hurt those close to me, Mr. Darcy. My feelings towards you are rooted in these actions and cannot be easily altered.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am well aware of the consequences of my actions, Elizabeth. My heart is troubled by them, yet it is my hope that through sincerity and time, I may earn your forgiveness and understanding.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I understand your desire for my forgiveness, Mr. Darcy, but I cannot pretend that my feelings have changed overnight. Your actions have consequences that extend beyond just words.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am not surprised by your words, Elizabeth. It is a task I have set myself to earn your esteem and respect, not merely your forgiveness.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I see, Mr. Darcy, that you are determined to change, but actions will speak louder than words. Prove to me and those I love that you have truly changed.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall endeavor to prove my sincerity and commitment to change, not just for your sake, Elizabeth, but for the sake of my own character.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I will await your actions, Mr. Darcy, and judge you by them. Until then, I must hold you accountable for your past.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I understand, Elizabeth. I shall do all in my power to earn your regard and the regard of your family.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I shall, Mr. Darcy. It is not my nature to hold grudges, but I cannot forget what you have done. Prove to me that you are indeed a changed man.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall, Elizabeth. My actions will be my testament. Until then, I ask only for your patience and understanding.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I shall watch your actions closely, Mr. Darcy, for they shall speak louder than your words.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall, Elizabeth. My actions shall indeed be my words.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: His misfortunes! yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
